REFUTED - THREE OF ITS FIVE SUB-CLAIMS ARE WRONG, AND ITS lane_impact WOULD SHIP BROKEN CONFIG. This is the contradiction lens paying out: it fights at least five already-upheld findings and it is the defective side. (1) CAPACITY IS WRONG. It says 'maxFocus = 48 + SPD*6' and calls 48 'the meter's FLOOR'. §1t1523s0§.as:2276 does return 48 + (SPD + gearSPD)*6, but that value is NOT maxreload. My grep for every assignment to §1t4415s0§ across the whole web bundle returns exactly two lines, §1t99s0§.as:249 and §1t4904s0§.as:77, and BOTH are 'this.§1t4415s0§ = 8 * 24;' = 192 flat. The 48+SPD*6 value is passed as the 7th argument of §1t1523s0§.as:2268 into §1t4443s0§ (§1t99s0§.as:183), whose android twin is MCSPlayer.initPlayer at :182 - and there it lands on a DIFFERENT field: :190 'this.baseReload = baseReload;'. My grep for 'baseReload' over MCSPlayer.as returns exactly three hits - the declaration at :105 'internal var baseReload:int = 48;', the parameter at :182, and the assignment at :190. Assigned, never read. DEAD CODE. maxreload is separately 'this.maxreload = 5 * 24;' at MCSPlayer.as:239. So the finding has swapped baseReload for maxreload, which is a different variable holding a different number. (2) REGEN IS WRONG. It says '+6 per call ... regen +6/tick'. The per-tick regen is §1t99s0§.as:1203-1205 'if(this.§1t4414s0§ < this.§1t4415s0§) { ++this.§1t4414s0§;' - PLUS ONE - and it pushes to the same HUD updater §1t5205s0§ at :1208. The '+= 6' at :3320 lives in §1t4479s0§, whose ONLY caller in the entire web bundle is §1t1543s0§.as:2049, inside 'if(_loc4_ > 0)' immediately before '§1t10181s0§ += _loc4_;'. I opened its android twin: NPCManager.as:1708-1711 is the identical statement pair with the names intact - 'if(deathCount > 0) { StatsManager.getPlayer().bonusReload(); }' then 'totalKilled += deathCount;'. The +6 is a KILL BONUS, not the tick regen. Shipping regen at +6 would run the crit meter six times fast. (3) THE SWITCH COST IS WRONG. It says 'changing stance costs nothing, it merely requires reload >= 48'. §1t99s0§.as:3162, inside the 'if(§1t1525s0§.§1t9948s0§())' battle guard, is 'this.§1t4414s0§ -= 48;' with a clamp at :3163-3166 and a HUD push at :3169. The in-battle switch charges a FLAT 48. WHAT SURVIVES: only the spend table (§1t99s0§.as:3299-3310, slashUsage x0.5 Light / x1 Balanced+Dual / x1.5 Heavy+Reversed) and the zero-on-full crit consumption (:3295-3297) - and both are already independently upheld, so nothing is lost by killing this. CONTRADICTED BY: [[skills-meters/maxreload-is-192]], [[combat-core/web-maxreload-192-and-48-offset]], [[combat-core/crit-meter-is-6-seconds]], [[skills-meters/focus-fill-rate-plus-one-per-frame]] ('the 48+SPD*6 value passed into the actor is dead code, assigned and never read'), [[hunter/focus-plus6-is-a-kill-bonus]], [[NF-A/web-focus-meter-constants-diverge-and-the-recharge-is-plus-one]], [[NF-B/web-focus-numerics-diverge-from-android-on-four-constants]] and [[progression/spd-scaling]], which correctly names 48+spd*6 'slash reload', not maxFocus. REFUTED — not for being incomplete, but because two of the numbers it ships as the contract are FALSE, and one of them is the exact quantity the blocker asks for. (2) 'regen +6/tick' is wrong. §1t99s0§.as:1203-1205 is the per-tick regen and it is '++this.§1t4414s0§' — plus ONE — pushed to the same HUD updater at :1208 (android MCSPlayer.as:1158-1160 identical). The +6 at :3320 is a KILL BONUS: its only caller is §1t1543s0§.as:2047-2049 'if(_loc4_ > 0) { ...§1t4479s0§(); }' where _loc4_ is the death count, and the android twin is literally named bonusReload, called from NPCManager.as:1709-1711 under 'if(deathCount > 0)'. new_findings.text: The in-combat stance switch is neither free nor forbidden: it COSTS 48 Focus, flat, in web v0.717. The stance setter §1t3489s0§ (§1t99s0§.as:3083) ends with 'if(§1t1525s0§.§1t9948s0§()) { this.§1t4414s0§ -= 48; if(this.§1t4414s0§ < 0) { this.§1t4414s0§ = 0; } ... §1t5205s0§(reload, maxreload); }' at :3160-3170. The android twin names the guard — MCSPlayer.as:3096 'if(StageManager.isBattle())' — and charges a DIFFERENT price: :3098-3105 'if(this.reload > this.maxreload / 2) { this.reload = this.maxreload / 3; } else { this.reload -= this.maxreload / 6; }'. Combined with the entry gate at §1t99s0§.as:3060 'if(this.§1t4414s0§ < 48) { return; }', the v0.717 rule is: you may cycle stance in combat iff Focus >= 48, and doing so spends exactly 48. This closes the 'switch-cost' third of RR:195 blocker (3) with a number, and it is the second, independent kill on RR:158-160 — the ledger has the in-combat switch as removed 2014 behaviour and a recreation divergence, when it is in the target build's own source with a price tag.

new_findings.text: The Focus/reload FILL TRIGGER — the thing RR:190 blocker (5) asks a human to watch the bar for — is in source, and it is three paths, not one. (a) PASSIVE: §1t99s0§.as:1203-1208, inside the per-tick update right after §1t3270s0§(), 'if(this.§1t4414s0§ < this.§1t4415s0§) { ++this.§1t4414s0§; ... §1t5205s0§(reload, maxreload); }' — plus ONE per tick, and it repaints the third HUD bar every tick. Android MCSPlayer.as:1158-1160 is identical. (b) ON KILL: the +6 at §1t99s0§.as:3320 is not a regen tick at all — its sole caller is §1t1543s0§.as:2047-2049 'if(_loc4_ > 0) { ...§1t4479s0§(); }' where _loc4_ is that pass's death count; the android twin is named bonusReload and is called from NPCManager.as:1709-1711 under 'if(deathCount > 0)'. So a kill (or a batch of them) is worth a flat +6. (c) SKILL: §1t120s0§.as:231 'param3.§1t4414s0§ = param3.§1t4415s0§ - 1;' (android SkillManager.as:218-219, 'case SKILL_FOCUS: owner.reload = owner.maxreload - 1;') — Replenish Focus fills the bar to maxreload MINUS ONE, i.e. it deliberately stops one point short of triggering the crit.

new_findings.text: RR:195 blocker (5) files the crit PROC rule as 'chance vs deterministic — entirely absent'. It is deterministic, and there is no dice roll anywhere near it. Web §1t99s0§.as:3272, inside the damage roll §1t4475s0§ (:3255), is 'if(this.§1t4414s0§ == this.§1t4415s0§)' -> ':3274 return _loc2_ * 1.3 + this.§1t1243s0§;'. Those two members are reload and maxreload: the android twin getDamage (MCSPlayer.as:3198) has the same test in plain English at :3215 'if(this.reload == this.maxreload)'. Crit fires exactly when the Focus meter is FULL, every time, and §1t99s0§.as:3295-3297 zeroes the meter on the next swing, so a full bar buys exactly one crit. Web v0.717 normalises it at 48: §1t113s0§.as:328 'var _loc3_:Number = (param1 - 48) / (param2 - 48);'. Android v0.682 normalises the SAME bar at 24: MCSPlayer.as:3272 'StageManager.getBattleUI().updateReload((this.reload - 24) / (this.maxreload - 24));' and :1163-1168 'this.tempreload = this.reload - 24; ... updateReload(this.tempreload / (this.maxreload - 24));'. Both builds compute the same capacity (48 + SPD*6: §1t1523s0§.as:2276 and android StatsManager.as:1841), so the divergence is purely in where the bar's zero point sits — and on web that zero point is the same 48 that gates the stance cycler.

verdicts.reason: HELD, and I reproduced BOTH halves first-hand. CODE: §1t113s0§.as:110 'this.§1t5203s0§ = "<font color=\'#000000\'>" + §1t1521s0§.getString(175) + "</font>";' and :111 the same with '#BBBBBB' + getString(960) - verbatim. :328 'var _loc3_:Number = (param1 - 48) / (param2 - 48);' then a strict three-way: :336 'if(_loc3_ == 0)' -> :340 shows the GREY string and :342 forces visible; :344 'else if(_loc3_ > 0 && _loc3_ < 1 ...)' -> :346 'this.§1t5169s0§.visible = false;'; :348 'else if(_loc3_ >= 1)' -> :352 Snd_criticalDamage + :356 the BLACK string. strings.json["175"] = 'Critical Hit'; the table has no key '960' (2,533 entries, checked programmatically). FRAME: I opened the frame and cut exactly the crop the finding states. Under a green 20/20 bar and a blue 26/26 bar sits a THIRD bar - a uniform dark gold/brown track with NO fill segment anywhere across its width - carrying 'CANNOT CHANGE STANCE' in light-grey caps, and the yellow '150% DAMAGE' buff sits BELOW the bar stack, not in it. Every visual particular the finding asserts is there. THE FRAME AND THE CODE DO NOT DISAGREE: an empty third bar is _loc3_ == 0, which is the only branch that shows that grey label, and the same meter at >= 48 opens §1t4470s0§. OVERTURN UPHELD: SHSD_MASTER_REFERENCE.md:388 reads verbatim '| **In combat** | **Hard lock** — "CANNOT CHANGE STANCE" appears the instant a fight starts | [CONTRACT] |', and :2099 repeats it; RR:158 carries the same bold claim. HELD on every number, and I independently settled the one thing the finding asserts without proving - that this meter is FOCUS. Verbatim: :249 'this.§1t4415s0§ = 8 * 24;' and :250 'this.§1t4414s0§ = 0;'; :1203 'if(this.§1t4414s0§ < this.§1t4415s0§)' -> :1205 '++this.§1t4414s0§;' with the HUD push at :1208 only when controlledBy == 0; :3162 'this.§1t4414s0§ -= 48;' clamped at :3163-3166; :3302 '-= this.slashUsage / 2', :3306 '-= this.slashUsage', :3310 '-= this.slashUsage * 1.5'; :3320 '+= 6' clamped to max. IDENTITY PROOF I ADDED: §1t120s0§.as:18 '§1t10128s0§:int = 1005;' and :230-231 'case §1t10128s0§: param3.§1t4414s0§ = param3.§1t4415s0§ - 1;'. skilldata.xml skill id 1005 carries <displayname>6008</displayname> and <desc>6011</desc>, and strings.json["6008"] = 'Focus', ["6011"] = 'Instantly recharges your focus bar.' The skill whose own description says it recharges the focus bar writes exactly this variable. §1t4414s0§ IS the Focus bar. Also checked and cleared a possible hole: §1t4419s0§ (param7, = baseReload = 48 + SPD*6 per §1t1523s0§.as:2274-2277) is assigned at :191 and never read on the player, so the flat +1/tick is the complete fill rule, not a partial one. OVERTURN UPHELD: RR:195 blocker (3) 'Focus numerics (max/fill/switch-cost)' names three quantities and the web payload hands over all three. The blocker falls. The finding labels its build correctly, so this is a note, not a defect.

PRIMARY CLAIM HELD, and I closed the gap the finding left open - it never proved the mastery scale caps at 10, it only pointed at a string. Verbatim: :3262 '_loc2_ = _loc1_ * (0.5 + 0.4 * this.§1t4421s0§ * 0.1);', :3265 '(1 + 0.2 * this.§1t4422s0§ * 0.1)', :3270 '_loc2_ = _loc1_ * 1.4;'. CAP PROVED TWO INDEPENDENT WAYS. (i) §1t1523s0§.as:2268 passes '§1t9714s0§(1000),§1t9714s0§(1001),§1t9714s0§(1002)' as params 12/13/14; the un-obfuscated Android twin StatsManager.as:1834 passes 'getStat(1000),getStat(1001),getStat(1002)' into the same 15-slot signature whose parameters MCSPlayer.as:182 names lightMastery/balancedMastery/heavyMastery. So mastery = the player's LEVEL in skills 1000/1001/1002. (ii) skilldata.xml gives skills 1000/1001/1002 (displaynames 6000/6002/6004 = Light/Balanced/Heavy Stance Mastery) exactly ten <level><value> rows, 1..10. So m in 0..10; m=10 -> 0.9 / 1.2 / 1.4, which is RR:155's ceiling table exactly; m=9 -> 0.86 / 1.18, which is nothing. OVERTURN UPHELD BUT NARROW: what falls in RR:155 is the two characters '-9'. The sentence's substance ('these are CEILING values, not base') SURVIVES intact, and the reach half of the same sentence (300/200/100) is untouched by this function - the finding's own PARTIAL verdict and lane_impact say so, which is why I am not treating it as an inflated overturn. The RR:157 fork ('decide-and-flag the build targets mastery-9') dissolves either way. ONE SUB-CLAIM REFUTED: 'Android ... on a 0-100 mastery scale' is WRONG. Android's masteries come from the same getStat(1000/1001/1002) 10-level skills, and MCSPlayer.as:3166-3168 gates perks at 'lightMastery >= 3 / >= 4 / >= 5', identical to web §1t99s0§.as:3223-3225 - thresholds of 3/4/5 are incoherent on a 0-100 scale. Android's divergence is the COEFFICIENT (0.01 vs 0.1) and the Heavy constant (1.5 vs 1.4), not the scale, which makes Android's Light cap 0.55 and its Balanced cap 1.05. The finding's conclusion ('must not be ported') survives and is in fact stronger than it claimed.

THE CLAIM IS TRUE; THE OVERTURN IS INFLATED. First, citelint flagged QUOTE_NOT_LOCATED - that flag is a formatting artifact, not a bad cite. I located both quoted lines verbatim: :3272 'if(this.§1t4414s0§ == this.§1t4415s0§)' and :3274 'return _loc2_ * 1.3 + this.§1t1243s0§;', with :3295-3297 zeroing the meter on the same equality. The cite RESOLVES on my own read. BUT: read RR:150-154 in context and the sentence the finding names does not fall - it is CONFIRMED. The ledger already writes 'Keep `CRIT_MULT=1.3`.' The code agrees with the ledger. Nothing there becomes false. What the evidence actually retires is (a) the parenthetical ACTION ITEM '(Read a real OG crit popup to fully seal it.)', which is an instruction, not a claim, and (b) two blockers on OTHER lines - RR:190 combat-core (2) 'crit 1.3 vs 3 final' and RR:195 skills-meters (5) 'crit proc rule (chance vs deterministic) - entirely absent'. Neither is the sentence in ledger_text. Worse for the overturn: RR:153's compounding explanation ('1.3x compounded with the per-stance crit-damage stat (Heavy x1.82) + item crit-damage') is CORROBORATED by this very code - 1.4 stance x 1.3 crit = 1.82 exactly, and §1t1243s0§ is the additive item crit-damage term, which Android names STAT_CRITICALDMG at MCSPlayer.as:3219. So the finding confirms the paragraph it claims to overturn. Real value, wrong target: promote CRIT_MULT=1.3 from wiki-authority to web-payload CONTRACT and close RR:190 (2) / RR:195 (5), but do NOT record RR:150-154 as overturned. In NodeGenerator the packed nodeid fields are literally named sectorx/sectory — A SECTOR IS A ROOM, one to one — and the containing unit is the TERRITORY. 'sector<->room mapping rule' names the wrong two levels; the real rule is territory<->room.

new_findings.text: The 6x6 territory rule is not a war-board special case, which is what the war-hex cite alone would support. NodeGenerator carries the general bidirectional transform, keyed on nothing but a raw nodeid, so it applies to town and wilderness alike: NodeGenerator.as:296-303 getTerritory and :305-312 getTerritoryId compute 'territoryx = Math.floor(sectorx / 6); territoryy = Math.floor(sectory / 6);' from the packed nodeid, and :314-320 getTerritorySector returns the within-territory offset as 'sectorx % 6' / 'sectory % 6'. Note the code's own vocabulary, which the ledger inverts: the packed nodeid fields are named sectorx/sectory — A SECTOR IS A ROOM, ONE TO ONE — and the 6x6 container is the TERRITORY. RR:225 blocker (5) is therefore named after the wrong two levels; the rule it asks for is territory<->room, and it is floor/modulo 6.

new_findings.text: RR:245 blocker (2) is 'War-Room map topology (board/adjacency)' — two halves — and the 6x6 finding argues only the board half, so the adjacency half would otherwise survive the rewrite. It does not. WarHexUI.as:443-463 getExitOwner IS the adjacency rule: it derives the territory's own war-map coordinates as 'territoryx = (this.mapid >> 12 & 0x0FFF) - 341' and 'territoryy = (this.mapid & 0x0FFF) - 341', then resolves each edge column and row to the neighbouring territory — xpos 0 to (territoryx - 1, territoryy), xpos 5 to (territoryx + 1, territoryy), ypos 0 to (territoryx, territoryy - 1), ypos 5 to (territoryx, territoryy + 1) — and returns 0 for interior cells. That is four-neighbour orthogonal territory adjacency with an explicit 341 coordinate origin, and it is what drives the frontline logic at :213-218 and :259-307. Both halves of RR:245 (2) fall together.

new_findings.text: The 271-cap finding kills RR:201's parenthetical but leaves its headline — 'The "271 cap" is gear/rebirth-inclusive' — standing. Both adjectives are false. GEAR: the panel's cap gate and the anti-cheat audit both read §1t9714s0§ (§1t5957s0§.as:3344, :3457), and §1t9714s0§ is getStat, proven by the android reinforce twin where §1t401s0§.as:1112 '§1t9714s0§(20064)' lines up with InteractUI.as:1104 'StatsManager.getStat(20064)'. Gear bonuses ride a SEPARATE accessor, §1t7358s0§ / findBonusStat, which is added on at the point of use — §1t1523s0§.as:2336 '§1t7356s0§(§1t9410s0§) + §1t7358s0§(§1t9410s0§)' — and never enters the cap comparison. REBIRTH: StatsManager.as:2135 sets the stat budget to '(getLevel() - 1) * 3' with no STAT_DAN term, in pointed contrast to the skill budget twenty lines later at :2156, 'getLevel() - 1 + getPlayerStats(STAT_DAN) * (levelCap - 1)', which does carry one. Rebirth multiplies SKILL points, not STAT points. 271 is a plain base-stat ceiling: 1 + (level + 10) * 3.

new_findings.text: The coins finding proves what the payout multipliers are (1x for loot type 0, 5x for type 1) but not where the type, quantity and probability come from, which is what 'coins-per-kill reality' actually asks. The roll is at §1t68s0§.as:820-828: it walks 'this.reward.loot', taking the type from §1t760s0§(), the count from getQty() and the probability from 'chance * 100', firing when '_loc6_ == 100 || Math.random() * 100 < _loc6_'. The rows themselves are in the NPC data — reference/extracted/npcdata.xml:39-42 is a real one, '<loot><id>0</id><qty>2</qty><chance>0.5</chance>', i.e. 2 coins on a coin-flip, and the file carries 131 <loot> blocks across its 495 npc rows. So per-kill coin income is fully tabulated, per enemy, not a constant awaiting measurement. Build caveat, stated plainly: the payout CODE is web v0.717, but npcdata.xml is android-sourced under C2, so the per-NPC rows are v0.682 until a web-side artifact says otherwise.
